- [ASSISTANT_SAID] VFX workflows involve processes and techniques used to create, manipulate, and integrate digital imagery into live-action footage.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The pre-production phase involves planning where VFX artists work with directors, producers, and cinematographers to determine the VFX needs for the project.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Asset creation involves creating digital assets such as characters, props, and environments using 3D modeling and texturing software.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Animation includes animating digital characters, objects, and environments through keyframe animation, motion capture, and simulations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Compositing is the process of combining different visual elements, such as live-action footage, CG elements, and visual effects, into a single cohesive image.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Rendering is the process of generating the final output of the visual effects, involving rendering individual elements and compositing them together.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Review and approval is the process of reviewing the visual effects work with the director and other stakeholders to ensure it meets the creative vision of the project.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Delivery is the final stage of the VFX workflow where the finished visual effects are delivered to the client or integrated into the final project.
